name: Sir Elton John
current_role: Singer-songwriter; founder, Elton John AIDS Foundation; co-owner of Rocket Entertainment
profile: English singer, pianist and composer (born Reginald Dwight, 1947) whose catalogue, touring and Rocket Entertainment business built his fortune. His Farewell Yellow Brick Road tour sold 6m+ tickets over 330 shows (2018-2023); he returned for Rock in Rio (Sept 2026) and two final Mexico City shows in October 2026. He is an EGOT winner and runs the Elton John AIDS Foundation.
interesting_fact: His Farewell Yellow Brick Road tour (2018-2023) sold over six million tickets across 330 shows, ending in Stockholm in July 2023, before he announced two extra 'farewell' shows in Mexico City for October 2026.
deep_cut_fact: At 15 he got his first paid gig as the pub pianist at the Northwood Hills Hotel near Pinner, playing Thursday to Sunday nights; he left Pinner County Grammar School just before his A-levels to pursue music.
notes: Musician rather than entrepreneur/energy figure; best route is the EJAF media office (foundation emails are for the foundation, not him personally) or Rocket Entertainment management.

name: Nick Leslau
current_role: Partner, Prestbury Capital Partners Ltd; chairman/CEO, Prestbury Investment Holdings (London)
profile: London commercial property investor (b. 1959, Cricklewood) who built Burford Holdings with Nigel Wray, then Prestbury Group, Max Property Group (sold to Blackstone 2014) and Secure Income REIT (Travelodge hotels, private hospitals, theme-park freeholds), which merged with LXI REIT in 2022. He now runs Prestbury Capital Partners with long-time partners Ben Walford and Sandy Gumm.
interesting_fact: Secure Income REIT, his long-income vehicle listed in 2014, owned 20 private hospitals and 55 Travelodge hotels before its 2022 merger with LXI REIT at a 16.5% average annual return.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of a German degree at Warwick to study quantity surveying, qualified as a chartered surveyor, and became CEO of Burford Estate & Property at just 23.
notes: Low media profile but gave an FT 'My money' interview (2015). Prestbury's general enquiries inbox is the published route.

name: Mo Jianrong
current_role: Linked by Hurun to Boee Group (保亿集团), Hangzhou property developer; exact current title not confirmed
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2012-2018) for Boee, i.e. Boee Group (保亿集团), a Hangzhou-based private developer founded on 16 Sept 1991 as Huarong home-appliance trading company in Taizhou that moved into real estate in the late 1990s. The group now spans property development, property management, trading and industrial investment. A third-party profile names a Mo Jianrong as chairman of its property-service arm.
interesting_fact: Boee began in 1991 as Zhejiang Huarong, a home-appliance trading firm, and switched to property; its first project, Boee Mingzhu in Taizhou (2001), made its name. Its property arm sent butlers to train in Europe for a 'platinum butler' service.
notes: Chairman's name on Boee's site is shown only as an image; a third-party site (altss.com) names founder Mo Jianhua as group chairman and Mo Jianrong as chairman of Zhejiang Boee Property Service - unverified. Group HQ: Boee Center, Qianjiang Century City, Hangzhou. Very private; Chinese-language media is the likely route.

name: Wang Yangang
current_role: Former chairman and CEO, China Animal Healthcare Ltd (HKEX: 0940); no current public role found
profile: Controlling shareholder, chairman and CEO of China Animal Healthcare, a veterinary-vaccine and animal-drug maker (incl. Inner Mongolia Bigvet Bio-tech) that listed via Singapore in 2007 and moved to Hong Kong in 2010. Hurun listed him with Li Chunhua (2014-2016). He stepped down from all board roles in July 2017; the shares were suspended in 2015 and the listing cancelled in January 2020.
interesting_fact: China Animal Healthcare was one of the few Chinese veterinary-vaccine makers to list overseas, first via a 2007 reverse takeover in Singapore before transferring to the Hong Kong main board in 2010.
notes: Name also romanised Wang Yan Gang in HKEX filings. Company delisted (2020) after a long suspension, and he has kept no public profile since leaving in 2017; no published contacts. Probably a poor podcast target.

name: Dmytro Firtash
current_role: Head of the board of directors, Group DF (chemicals/fertiliser, gas distribution, titanium, media)
profile: Ukrainian businessman (b. 1965, Ternopil Oblast) who began in barter trading after military service, became co-owner of gas trader RosUkrEnergo, and in 2007 consolidated holdings into Group DF: Ostchem nitrogen plants, regional gas distribution, titanium and the Inter TV channel. He has lived in Vienna since 2014 contesting US extradition and is under Ukrainian sanctions.
interesting_fact: In 2014 he bought the disused Brompton Road tube station in London from the UK Ministry of Defence for about £53m, planning to convert it into flats.
deep_cut_fact: His donations helped Cambridge University create its Cambridge Ukrainian Studies programme (2008) and, in 2012, Cambridge-Ukraine studentships for Ukrainian master's students; a 2010 gift was reported at $6.7m.
notes: Highly controversial: under US federal indictment (fighting extradition from Austria since 2014) and sanctioned by Ukraine (2021). Reputational risk for a podcast; journalist should weigh this. Group DF press office is the only published route.

name: Christina Tan
current_role: Executive Chairman, MT Maritime Management (USA) LLC; independent director, Dorian LPG (NYSE: LPG) and Pangaea Logistics Solutions (NASDAQ: PANL)
profile: Shipping executive (age 73 per 2026 proxy) who has spent 30+ years at the MT Maritime Management (MTM) Group in finance and chartering, rising to CEO and now Executive Chairman of its US arm. She has sat on Dorian LPG's board since May 2015 and on Pangaea Logistics' board; her SEC-reported holdings stem from those insider positions.
interesting_fact: Before shipping, she spent eight years as VP of Finance & Trading at Socoil Corporation, a major Malaysian palm-oil refiner and trader.
deep_cut_fact: She earned a BA in Economics and Mathematics from Western State College of Colorado (now Western Colorado University in Gunnison), and served on the board of Northern Shipping Funds (2008-2015) and its LP advisory committee until 2023.
notes: Low public profile; LPG shipping (Dorian) is energy-adjacent. Best route is via Dorian LPG investor relations or MTM Group. Net-worth figure is from SEC insider holdings and may reflect shares held through affiliated entities.

name: Lui Wing Chi
current_role: Chairman & Executive Director, S E A Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 0251)
profile: Lu (Lui) Wing Chi, Jesse, chairs S E A Group, one of Hong Kong's longest-established property developers (founded 1956), which he joined in 1969. The group has developed 200+ projects across Hong Kong, mainland China, the UK, Australia and New Zealand and holds London offices such as 33 Old Broad Street and 20 Moorgate. Recent Hong Kong projects include Grand Victoria in West Kowloon and The Cendas office tower in Kowloon East.
interesting_fact: S E A's consortium won the West Kowloon waterfront residential site (now Grand Victoria) at a record HK$17.3bn, and the group sold its Wan Chai tower at 108 Gloucester Road to China Everbright for about HK$10bn.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the family group in 1969, when its experience included godown (warehouse) and factory operations, before it became an international office and residential developer; in 2022 it set a government-tender record with a HK$1.18bn Repulse Bay waterfront site.
notes: Hurun lists him as 吕荣梓; company uses 'Lu Wing Chi'. Day-to-day leadership sits with Chief Executive Lambert Lu. Company general inbox is the published route; low personal media profile.

name: Xiang Lehong
current_role: Chairman, Loctek Ergonomic Technology Corp. (乐歌股份, SZSE: 300729), Ningbo
profile: Founder-chairman of Loctek, which began in March 2002 as Lijing Electronic Cable in Ningbo and became a maker of electric sit-stand desks, monitor arms and smart beds. It listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in Dec 2017 as the first A-share ergonomics company and the first cross-border e-commerce IPO, and now also runs public overseas warehouses for Chinese brands shipping abroad. Hurun lists him with Lou Yi.
interesting_fact: Loctek invested over US$100m in public overseas-warehouse complexes, turning a desk maker into a cross-border logistics provider ('4supply') for other Chinese brands.
deep_cut_fact: At the 'cloud opening' of the 127th Canton Fair (2020, held online), Xiang Lehong was the company chairman who video-linked live with then-Premier Li Keqiang; Loctek was also first to put electric height-adjustment into a children's study desk.
notes: Listed-company chairman; IR contact is published in Loctek's SZSE filings (investor-relations page on loctek.com is JS-only). Cross-border e-commerce/logistics angle may suit an entrepreneurship podcast.

current_role: Founder/controlling shareholder (reported chairman), Xin Point Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 1571), Huizhou

deep_cut_fact: Cheersson's fastener subsidiary invested RMB260m in a plant designed to make 3 billion fasteners a year for 5G telecom gear and EV battery packs, announced in its IPO year, 2020.
notes: Energy-storage/EV battery-structure parts give an energy angle. Company general inbox is the only published email; IR contact is in SZSE filings.

name: Zhao Lijun
current_role: Founder and long-time chairman of Poten Environment Group (博天环境); current role after 2022 restructuring not confirmed
profile: Beijing water-treatment entrepreneur behind Poten Environment, which began on 18 Jan 1995 as Beijing Boda Environmental Engineering, passed through state, foreign and private ownership, and listed in Shanghai (603603) in 2017. Poten treats industrial and municipal water and does ecological restoration; after a 2022 court-approved restructuring its shares moved to the delisted-company board (400210).
interesting_fact: Poten has pivoted toward green hydrogen: its subsidiary Tianji Hydrogen (est. 2019) does hydrogen system integration and in 2024 signed a project with Changshu High-tech Zone.
deep_cut_fact: Poten was twice (4th and 5th terms) the presiding member company of the Environment Chamber of Commerce of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce.
notes: Company went through bankruptcy restructuring (2022) and was delisted from Shanghai; check whether Zhao still controls or chairs it before outreach. Hydrogen/water angle is relevant to energy podcast but approach with care.

name: Xiao Wei
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu Kanion Pharmaceutical Co. (康缘药业, SSE: 600557), Lianyungang; Academician, Chinese Academy of Engineering
profile: Scientist-entrepreneur with a PhD in Chinese materia medica who chairs Kanion, a large modern traditional-Chinese-medicine maker with 61 approved new TCM drugs, 800+ invention patents and 27 exclusive drugs on China's national reimbursement list. He has researched TCM drug creation, process quality control and intelligent manufacturing for 40+ years and has been a National People's Congress deputy in four consecutive terms (11th-14th).
interesting_fact: He is both a listed-company chairman and an academician of the Chinese Academy of Engineering, and served as chief scientist on a national '973' basic-research programme.
deep_cut_fact: He directs China's National Key Laboratory for TCM pharmaceutical process control and intelligent manufacturing, is an executive member of the Chinese Pharmacopoeia Commission, and won the Ho Leung Ho Lee Foundation science and innovation prize and the Guanghua Engineering Science and Technology Prize.
notes: Strong 'smart manufacturing' and science angle. No published email found on the site; investor-relations contacts are in Kanion's SSE filings.
